title: THE DEVIL IS IN THE NEURONS: INTERPRETING AND MITIGATING SOCIAL BIASES IN PRE-TRAINED LANGUAGE MODELS
findings: Religion was one of nine demographic dimensions analyzed for social bias. The study found that their proposed method (IG²) could identify a specific number of 'social bias neurons' associated with the religion dimension (an average of 1.20 in BERT). Their debiasing technique (BNS) was shown to mitigate these biases across dimensions, including religion, by suppressing these identified neurons. However, the paper does not provide detailed quantitative results or specific stereotypes related to religion, focusing instead on the general methodology's effectiveness.

measurement_description: The benchmark was designed to measure social bias in pre-trained language models. For religion, it specifically measured the fairness gap and biased associations by comparing model predictions for pairs of religious demographics (Islam-Christianity, Muslim-Catholic) within template-based, fill-in-the-blank prompts.
